howDoI.q: How do I make a monster pay points when Yana touches it?
How do I make a touched monster turn into a number?
How do I make a number float up and go away?
How do I make a number blink?
How do I draw a number like 200 or 500?
How do I stop a number from staying on the screen?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Score Popups is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

When you score, a number rises and fades. Game-Maker has no command for that. It is a monster, and this game builds it. Nothing here hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: A Number Appears
pages.html:
Level 1: A Number Appears

The first sign says PLAIN COINS JUST VANISH. Walk over the two coins on the ground: each pays 10 points and is gone, and nothing else happens.

The THESE COINS ARE MONSTERS sign points at three spinning gold coins. Touch one. It pays 100 points, and a blinking 100 floats up where it was, then goes. The next sign says what you just saw.

One of the three coins hangs at Yana's head and two stand at her feet. All of them are taken just by walking.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A prize that is a monster. Open pop.mon in the monsters editor and pick the coin. It has no path, so it hangs in the air and spins between two pictures. Its Power is 50. A monster under 100 is destroyed when Yana touches it; at 100 or more Yana walks through it and nothing happens.
  • The points. Open pop.mbl in the blocks editor and pick coin0. Its Score points is 100, and so is coin1's, so it pays on either frame. The score comes from the picture that is touched. The monster's own Score when destroyed by a weapon is for thrown things and does nothing here.
  • The number. The coin's When destroyed it becomes is POP100. The new monster is born in the same place, the same tick.
  • Blinking. POP100 shows two pictures one after the other: num100 for 4 ticks and empty, a picture with nothing in it, for 3. The eye sees a blink.
  • Rising and leaving. Its Movement path is one corner, two blocks up at speed 1, and its Lives is Until the end of its path. When it has risen two blocks it is destroyed. Power 150 keeps Yana's touch from doing anything to it.
  • The map. Open one.map: the three coins are monsters put on the map, and the two plain coins are blocks.

pages.head: Level 2: Its Own Picture
pages.html:
Level 2: Its Own Picture

The EACH NUMBER IS ITS OWN PICTURE sign stands before a blue gem and an orange box. The gem pays 200 and shows a 200. The box pays 500 and shows a 500. They are three different pictures.

The THIS 100 NEVER GOES AWAY sign points at one more coin. It pays 100, but its number blinks in place and does not leave. That is the mistake to learn from. Walk on through it: it is not solid and pays nothing.

The LET ITS PATH END TO CLEAR IT sign comes before the last coin, which is built the right way and rises and goes.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Three numbers, three pictures. A number is a 20 by 20 picture in pop.mbl: num100, num200 and num500. Game-Maker has no way to print the score, so every number you want to float up must be drawn. The digits in this game are five pixels wide with a one-pixel outline.
  • Three prizes. The gem and box are made like the coin, each with its own Score points and its own When destroyed it becomes.
  • The mistake. The stuck coin is a second coin monster that becomes STUCKPOP. Its Lives is Forever (indestructible) and it has no Movement path, so nothing ever removes it.
  • The fix. The last coin becomes POP100, whose Lives is Until the end of its path. Either a path that ends or For a set time clears a number.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in pop.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A popup is a picture, and that is all it can be:

  • It cannot draw a number. It cannot show the score, a count or the points a prize happened to pay. Every number is a picture you draw, one monster each, and a game that pays 10, 20 and 50 draws three.
  • It cannot take a value from the touch. The prize pays what its picture's Score points says and becomes the one monster you named.
  • A monster is born on the spot of the thing it replaces, never beside it or above it. To start a number higher, give it a path that begins by moving.
  • At most 200 monsters are alive at once, popups included, so a crowd of them can leave no room for a new one.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Change the number's path from 2 blocks up to 4. It floats higher.
  • Make num100's picture show for 8 ticks. It blinks more slowly.
  • Draw a 1000 in the blocks editor, add a monster that shows it, and make the box become it.
  • Give a prize a set Score points of 1000 and leave its number at 100, and see how a number can lie. Better to match them.
  • Fix the stuck coin: set the stuck number's Lives to Until the end of its path and give it a path.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
